Circular Heatmap of Beta Values

Source: R/module_plotting.R
BetaCircularHeatmap.Rd

Generates a circular/radial heatmap visualization of beta values using ComplexHeatmap and circlize packages.

Usage

BetaCircularHeatmap(
  beta,
  meta = NULL,
  probes.all = NULL,
  probeset = NULL,
  genome = "hg38",
  version = toupper(genome),
  SAMPLEID = "Sample_Name",
  sectionColumn = "Sample_Group",
  sectionLabels = NULL,
  outFile = NULL,
  nchars = 5,
  format = NULL,
  res = 300
)

Arguments

beta

Matrix or data.frame of beta values (rows = probes, columns = samples).

meta

Optional data.frame of sample metadata with SAMPLEID column.

probes.all

Optional probe annotation data.

probeset

Character scalar for probeset name or NULL.

genome

Genome build of the probeset coordinates, "hg38" (default) or "hg19".

version

Coordinate columns used from probes.all (CHR_<version>, MAPINFO_<version>); defaults to the upper-case genome.

SAMPLEID

Column name for sample identifiers (default "Sample_Name").

sectionColumn

Column name for grouping samples into sections. Use "Sample_Name" to show each sample as its own section, or "Sample_Group" to group multiple samples. Circular heatmaps work best with 1-5 sections.

sectionLabels

Optional custom section labels.

outFile

Optional output file path. The extension selects the format when format is NULL: .png writes a raster image, anything else a vector PDF.

nchars

Number of characters to show in gene labels (default 5). Note: This applies to gene names only, not group labels which are shown in full.

format

Output format, "pdf" (vector) or "png" (raster), or NULL (default) to infer it from outFile. Raster output keeps file size independent of the numbers of probes and samples, which suits large cohorts.

res

Resolution in dots per inch for raster output (default 300).

Value

Invisibly returns the heatmap object.

Details

Crowding considerations:

  • Circular heatmaps are optimized for small numbers of samples (1-5 per section).

  • For 5-10+ samples per section, consider using plot_type = "heatmap_by_probe" instead (rectangular heatmap) which handles many samples better.

  • Each section represents a unique value in sectionColumn.
